trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: Baseline net, more updates
trials.hypothesis: This keeps the starting network and only changes the recipe. With 128 envs x 16 steps per update, training gets 64 updates instead of 32, and twice as many gradient steps (16 minibatches of 128 samples). With only 131k steps, the policy's progress is likely limited by the number of updates, not by how noisy each update is. It is refuted if dev success is no better than the starting architecture's, or is less stable across seeds.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: Footprint-pooled placement head
trials.hypothesis: This keeps the 2-layer body and the more-updates recipe, but replaces the 1x1 placement head. For each brick type, learned features are max- and min-pooled over that type's footprint (anchored at its top-left cell), and a small per-type MLP gives the logit. The landing layer is the highest point under the footprint, and a placement is correct only if every footprint cell matches the target, so the pooling fits the task. It is refuted if this does no better than the same recipe with the plain 1x1 head.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: Residual body, global context, footprint head
trials.hypothesis: This uses a width-48 stem plus 2 residual blocks (receptive field about 11x11). Each block adds a broadcast of globally pooled features, and the footprint-pooled head is kept. Placement order (supports before overhangs, when to choose DONE) depends on the whole grid. PPO epochs drop to 2, which roughly offsets the extra compute in samples. It is refuted if this does no better than the footprint-head candidate with the 2-layer body.

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: Footprint head, longer horizon
trials.hypothesis: This keeps r1c2 exactly and changes only gamma (0.95 to 0.99) and gae_lambda (0.9 to 0.95). The +1 exact-build bonus arrives at the end of the episode. With gamma 0.95 it is discounted about 5x after 30 steps, so the policy is barely rewarded for finishing exactly or for choosing DONE at the right time. A longer horizon should raise exact-build success. It is refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.48.

trials.label: r2c2
trials.name: Footprint head with obs skip
trials.hypothesis: This keeps r1c2 but adds a learned 1x1 projection of the raw observation. It is concatenated with the body features before the footprint max/min pooling. Landing height and whether a placement fills or seals the right cells depend on exact per-cell layer and height values, which two 3x3 convolutions blur. Pooling sharp per-cell features over each footprint should make placement scoring more precise, at almost no extra compute. It is refuted if dev success is not above about 0.50.

trials.label: r2c3
trials.name: Deeper dilated body, equal compute
trials.hypothesis: This replaces r1c2's two width-64 convolutions with three width-48 convolutions, the last one with dilation 2. Compute stays about the same (around 1.3x the start), so the sample budget is unchanged, while the view of the grid grows from 5x5 to 9x9 cells. Deciding placement order (supports before overhangs, not sealing cells the target needs) depends on a wider area. PPO epochs stay at 4, unlike r1c3. It is refuted if dev success is not above about 0.50.

trials.label: r3c1
trials.name: Obs skip + dilated body
trials.hypothesis: Takes r2c2 (footprint head with obs skip) and swaps its body for r2c3's three width-48 convolutions, the last one dilated. The wider 9x9 view should help with placement order, while the skip keeps sharp per-cell features. The two changes address different weaknesses, so they should add up. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is not above about 0.56, or if seed spread stays as large as r2c2's.

trials.label: r3c2
trials.name: r2c2 with double updates
trials.hypothesis: Keeps the r2c2 network and changes only the recipe: n_envs drops from 128 to 64 and n_minibatches from 16 to 8. Minibatches stay at 128 samples, and the number of PPO updates doubles from about 40 to about 80 at the same compute. Train success matches dev success, so learning is held back by the number of optimisation steps, not by overfitting. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is not above about 0.57, or if both seeds fall below 0.5.

trials.label: r3c3
trials.name: Per-layer footprint pooling
trials.hypothesis: Adds a branch to r2c2's head. A small 1x1 encoder, shared across layers, reads each layer's build, target, missing and extra cells plus the column heights and a layer-index channel. Its output is max/min-pooled over each footprint separately for each layer. A placement is correct only if the landing layer is missing in every footprint cell and no target cell is sealed below. These are per-layer AND/OR tests over the footprint, which this branch exposes directly. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is not above about 0.57.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
LK = 8

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16}


def fp_pool(t, dy, dx):
    if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
        p = F.pad(t, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
        mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
        mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
        return mx, mn
    return t, t


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1)
        self.skip = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, PROJ, 1)
        self.layer_enc = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(7, LK, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(LK, LK, 1), nn.ReLU()
        )
        n_in = 6 * PROJ + 3 * self.Z * LK
        self.mlps = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(n_in, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps
        ])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        f = self.body(obs)
        g = F.relu(torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.skip(obs)], dim=1))
        per = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X).permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4)
        hts = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 2].unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, 2, Y, X)
        zpos = torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / max(Z - 1, 1)
        zpos = zpos.view(1, Z, 1, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, 1, Y, X)
        lay = torch.cat([per, hts, zpos], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 7, Y, X)
        h = self.layer_enc(lay)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), mlp in zip(self.fps, self.mlps):
            gmx, gmn = fp_pool(g, dy, dx)
            hmx, hmn = fp_pool(h, dy, dx)
            lf = torch.cat([h, hmx, hmn], dim=1).reshape(B, Z * 3 * LK, Y, X)
            outs.append(mlp(torch.cat([g, gmx, gmn, lf], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        gl = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gl)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gl).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: Keeps the r3c2 network and lowers ppo_epochs from 4 to 2. The sample budget rises from about 83k to about 155k steps (about 150 updates), while total gradient steps stay about the same. trials.label: r4c2

trials.hypothesis: Replaces r3c2's linear 1x1 obs skip with a 2-layer 1x1 MLP (27 to 64 to 32). Whether a placement fills missing cells depends on the target and missing bits at the build's current height. That is a per-cell interaction between layers and heights, which a linear map cannot form before footprint pooling. The extra compute is tiny. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.57.

Placement order depends on the state of the whole grid: build lower layers before overhangs, and finish areas that are nearly complete. The local 5x5 view cannot see this, and the change costs almost no compute. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.57.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8}


class FootprintHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, c_obs, c_glob, footprints):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, PROJ, 1)
        self.skip = nn.Conv2d(c_obs, PROJ, 1)
        self.first = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(6 * PROJ, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.ctx = nn.ModuleList([nn.Linear(c_glob, HID) for _ in self.fps])
        self.last = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f, obs, gvec):
        g = F.relu(torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.skip(obs)], dim=1))
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
                p = F.pad(g, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            else:
                mx = g
                mn = g
            h = self.first[i](torch.cat([g, mx, mn], dim=1))
            h = F.relu(h + self.ctx[i](gvec)[:, :, None, None])
            outs.append(self.last[i](h))
        return torch.cat(outs, dim=1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = FootprintHead(WIDTH, spec.in_channels, WIDTH, spec.footprints)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        place = self.place_head(f, obs, g).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8}


class FootprintHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, c_obs, c_glob, footprints):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, PROJ, 1)
        self.skip = nn.Conv2d(c_obs, PROJ, 1)
        self.first = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(6 * PROJ, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.ctx = nn.ModuleList([nn.Linear(c_glob, HID) for _ in self.fps])
        self.last = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f, obs, gvec):
        g = F.relu(torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.skip(obs)], dim=1))
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
                p = F.pad(g, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            else:
                mx = g
                mn = g
            h = self.first[i](torch.cat([g, mx, mn], dim=1))
            h = F.relu(h + self.ctx[i](gvec)[:, :, None, None])
            outs.append(self.last[i](h))
        return torch.cat(outs, dim=1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.body_ctx = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.place_head = FootprintHead(WIDTH, spec.in_channels, WIDTH, spec.footprints)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h1 = F.relu(self.conv1(obs))
        c1 = self.body_ctx(torch.cat([h1.mean((2, 3)), h1.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f = F.relu(self.conv2(F.relu(h1 + c1[:, :, None, None])))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        place = self.place_head(f, obs, g).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
HEADS = 4

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8}


class FootprintHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, c_obs, c_glob, footprints):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, PROJ, 1)
        self.skip = nn.Conv2d(c_obs, PROJ, 1)
        self.first = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(6 * PROJ, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.ctx = nn.ModuleList([nn.Linear(c_glob, HID) for _ in self.fps])
        self.last = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        for m in self.last:
            nn.init.zeros_(m.weight)
            nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)

    def forward(self, f, obs, gvec):
        g = F.relu(torch.cat([self.proj(f), self.skip(obs)], dim=1))
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
                p = F.pad(g, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            else:
                mx = g
                mn = g
            h = self.first[i](torch.cat([g, mx, mn], dim=1))
            h = F.relu(h + self.ctx[i](gvec)[:, :, None, None])
            outs.append(self.last[i](h))
        return torch.cat(outs, dim=1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(WIDTH)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(WIDTH, HEADS, batch_first=True)
        self.place_head = FootprintHead(WIDTH, spec.in_channels, WIDTH, spec.footprints)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        f = self.body(obs)
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        tn = self.norm(t)
        a, _ = self.attn(tn, tn, tn, need_weights=False)
        t = t + a
        f = t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, WIDTH, Y, X)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        place = self.place_head(f, obs, g).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1:
There are no results yet, and success scores stay hidden for the whole search. Each candidate therefore has to stand on its own as a plausible improvement, and the three should differ from each other.

The default recipe gets only 32 PPO updates (131,072 steps at 4,096 per update), which looks too few for a 401-action policy. Smaller updates give more learning steps for the same compute.

In the starting network, each logit comes from a 1x1 conv on features at the brick's top-left anchor cell only. A brick lands one layer above the highest cell under its footprint, so the network should help by pooling learned features over each brick type's footprint (both max and min).

Ordering decisions, such as placing supports before an overhang and choosing when to stop (DONE), need context from the whole grid. A deeper residual body with global pooled context can supply it. To limit the sample loss from the larger network, that candidate uses 2 PPO epochs instead of 4.
analyses.2: The footprint-pooled placement head is the one big win so far: 0.51, with both seeds near 0.5, against 0.07 for the 1x1 head under the same recipe. That gap is far larger than seed noise. The score 0.068 looks like a failure basin that seeds can fall into. The residual body with global context and 2 PPO epochs hit that basin on one seed (0.068 and 0.41). That trial changed three things at once (depth, context, epochs), so it does not tell us whether depth helps. Changing only the recipe on the plain net did nothing. Next steps, each a single change on r1c2: (a) a longer reward horizon, because the +1 exact-build bonus comes at the end of up to 41 steps and gamma 0.95 discounts it heavily; (b) giving the footprint head precise per-cell observation features, because landing and overhang checks need exact cells; (c) a deeper body at about the same compute, to see whether a larger view of the grid helps decide placement order.
analyses.3: The footprint-pooled head is the one big effect (0.07 to about 0.51) and has worked on almost every seed. Every change since then is within seed noise. The obs skip (r2c2, 0.574) has the best mean but its seeds spread widely (0.70 and 0.45). The dilated 3-layer body (r2c3, 0.537) was steady across seeds. Gamma 0.99 did not help, so I am dropping horizon changes. Training uses about 100s of the 900s limit, and train success is close to dev success, so the agent is limited by learning rather than overfitting. Sample count and how efficiently features are learned matter most. Next steps: (1) combine the obs skip with the dilated body, since the two changes may add up; (2) double the number of PPO updates with the r2c2 net; (3) test a task-structured idea: per-layer features pooled over each footprint, so the head can directly see the landing layer and whether a placement fills or seals target cells.
analyses.4: The footprint-pooled placement head is the only large, reliable gain so far (0.07 to about 0.51). Since then, everything has landed between 0.47 and 0.59. These include the obs skip (0.574), double updates (0.590), the dilated body (0.537), skip plus dilation (0.475) and gamma 0.99 (0.478). Per-seed spread is about ±0.14, so most of these differences are noise. The per-layer pooling run (0.371) and the residual body with 2 epochs (0.239) are clearly worse. Both used more compute, which left fewer samples, and the residual run had one seed collapse to 0.068. Train success tracks dev success, so the agent is not overfitting. It is short of samples, optimisation steps or precise features. This round makes 3 single changes to r3c2. The first is a recipe change: 2 PPO epochs give about 1.9x more fresh samples for roughly the same number of gradient steps. The second is a cheap nonlinear per-cell skip, so the head can see interactions between layers and heights before pooling. The third broadcasts the global context into the placement head, to help with ordering.
analyses.5: Pooling learned features over each brick's footprint gave the biggest gain (0.07 to 0.51). The obs skip (0.57) and global context in the placement head (r4c3, 0.65) each added a smaller one. r4c3 is also the most consistent across seeds (0.63 and 0.67). Its two seeds sit together, but a single seed can still swing about ±0.15. Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2 hurt badly (0.28), even with nearly twice the samples. So training seems limited by how much each sample is reused in optimisation, not by how many fresh designs it sees. This also explains r1c3's failure: it ran 2 epochs, so its residual body with global context was never tested fairly. Per-layer pooling, a nonlinear skip, the dilated body and a longer gamma did not help. Next tests: more epochs (6), global context inside the conv body, and a cheap self-attention layer that sees the whole grid.
